answers.answer: Roll one die per held office card simultaneously; add one for each fatigue on that card, and add one more for the Chairman. Modified 1–2 has no effect, 3–4 adds fatigue, and 5+ retires the officeholder. Move a retiree to Pensioners, flip the office card to Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to the supply.
answers.evidence: London Season: ‘Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire.’

answers.answer: Only players who retired at least one pensioner may take or discard a displayed card. They act in descending order of actual total retirement spending; ties go to most total windows including new prizes, then clockwise from the PM. The acting player may peek at display blackmails. Do not replace cards while selecting. If the display empties, skip all remaining eligible players immediately. After selection, discard all remaining display cards and refill exactly three (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown), even if nobody took one. Return every remaining Pensioner to the supply.
answers.evidence: London Season: ‘Players who retired at least one pensioner’; ‘descending actual total retirement spending’; ‘discarding all remaining cards and refilling exactly three.’

answers.answer: At the start of Family, a player chooses one action and puts their opportunity marker on it. If the marker was already on that action at phase start, the player may take that action twice. Only the latest passed extra-action law may be used; that extra action is not doubled by the marker and does not move it. With four vacant offices and the marker already on Enlist Writer, the doubled action places two writers, and the vacancy bonus adds one more writer once this turn: three total.
answers.evidence: Family: ‘If your marker was already on that action at phase start, you may take that action twice’; Enlist Writer: ‘With at least four vacant offices, place one additional writer once this turn.’

answers.answer: After all Family actions, if Debt and applicants both remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and reduce Debt by one; repeat while both remain. Those Court pieces are Company shares. If Debt is gone, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible while preserving their order. Seeking a share pays its listed cost to the bank, not to Company treasuries.
answers.evidence: Family: ‘move the rightmost applicant into Court and lower Debt by one’; ‘Seeking a share never pays family cash into Company treasuries.’

answers.answer: Hire vacancies in ascending order of the number on their card backs. For ordinary own-family hiring, every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool must verbally consent; Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt. When promoting an officeholder, transfer its fatigue to the new card and insert the old card, vacant, into ascending hiring order. If no candidate exists or the designated hirer is vacant, skip the office; it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.
answers.evidence: Hiring: ‘Fill vacant offices in ascending number’; Nepotism requires consent of ‘every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool’; fatigue transfers to new card.

answers.answer: The former Chairman first announces the number of shares needed for a pure majority (more than half of current shares). Shareholders may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. If nobody reaches that support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself, without Nepotism consent. The winning Company share moves into the Chairman slot and still counts as a share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in a firm.
answers.evidence: Chairman election: ‘first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins’; Chairman share ‘cannot be traded or invested in firms.’

answers.answer: Before a Company-office check, commit resources and cash; all cash comes from that acting office’s treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice and subtract penalties, then roll; the lowest die governs the result: 1–2 succeeds, 3–4 fails and may be retried if resources and office-specific limits allow, and 5–6 is catastrophic, ends that office’s actions, returns its officeholder to supply, discards its fatigue, and flips its card into Vacant Offices. Commander and firm procedures can modify this. Do not take a dead action with no effect or chance of success, such as trading with no ship or deploying with no dice just to trigger officer losses.
answers.evidence: Success checks: ‘all cash for a Company-office check comes from that acting office’s treasury and is paid to the bank’; ‘Use lowest die: 1–2 success; 3–4 failure, retry…; 5–6 catastrophic failure.’

answers.answer: The Chairman may freely borrow up to three advances, each adding £5 to Balance. Each additional advance needs consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares (counting the Chairman), and borrowing may never pass the Debt track end. The Chairman must allocate all Balance to other offices’ treasuries, reducing Balance by each transfer. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved while respecting those limits; cash already in office treasuries stays there for that office to use.
answers.evidence: Chairman: ‘May add up to three Debt freely, each +£5 Balance’; ‘Then allocate all Balance to other offices’ treasuries.’

answers.answer: The Manager of Shipping must spend its treasury until £2 or less remains. It may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without the owner’s consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Every acquired ship may be placed in any sea zone, including China once that office exists. Extra ships last only until Refresh.
answers.evidence: Manager of Shipping: ‘Must spend treasury until £2 or less remains’; Company ship purchase only ‘if no ships remain on shipyards.’

answers.answer: The President declares a set of regions that must include its home region and may include only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 from the President’s treasury buys one die; subtract one die per declared nonhome region. Failure may be retried during that President’s uninterrupted opportunity if affordable; catastrophe removes the President. A successful Trade may occur at most once per President per turn. On success, fill one order per ship in its sea zone, as many as possible within declared regions. Place the first writer at home, and each later order must be adjacent to an order already filled by that Presidency; use real writers while available, then filled-order tokens. A President cannot fill another President’s home region even if its office is vacant. Increase Balance by each order’s printed value, or half rounded down if a firm filled it this turn; the President gets £1 from the bank per order, and writer owners get £1 per writer placed. Separate adjacent writers from different Presidencies with dividers for Refresh.
answers.evidence: Presidency Trade: ‘include home region’; ‘subtract one per declared nonhome region’; ‘one successful Trade per President per turn’; successful trade rewards Balance, President and writers.

answers.answer: Deploy may target the Commander’s own Presidency home, any associated region, or any region bordering an associated region. It may not target another Presidency’s home or another Presidency’s Company-controlled region. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order for the action to have an effect. Exhaust officers and regiments for one die each and local alliances for their printed dice; subtract the strength of the target and all other regions in its empire, counting the target only once (Company defense strength is zero). A noncatastrophic failure can be retried with remaining resources. After every attempt, each owner rolls one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 removes that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll officer losses.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy: target restrictions; dice from exhausted pieces and alliances; subtract target empire strength; officer owners roll after each attempt.

answers.answer: On successful Deploy, loot is £4 per target tower plus the faceup loot token modifier, with a floor of one plus the number of surviving used officers. Pay £1 to the Commander plus £1 per its used surviving officer; pay £1 clockwise for each other player’s used surviving officer; then pay the bank £1 per regiment and per alliance piece regardless of alliance strength, repeating the cycle until the loot is gone. The Commander gains one trophy per target tower. Then remove the tower/dome; if the target was a capital, remove all matching empire flags; open its orders and clear unrest. If it becomes Company-controlled, put the loot/control token region-side above the President and put a Governor overlay in the region, with only the office card placed in Vacant Offices. If the Elephant was there pointing outward, move it fully inside. On catastrophic failure the Commander returns half their family’s trophies, rounded up, and the Commander member goes to supply; exhausted officers still check losses, and there is no office card to vacate.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy: ‘loot = £4 per target tower + faceup loot token’s modifier’; ‘one trophy per target tower’; catastrophe returns half trophies rounded up.

answers.answer: The Governor takes its printed dice pool and makes attempts without a penalty, reducing the pool by one after every result. Success pays £1, plus another £1 if the previous roll was unsuccessful, and the Governor chooses to build a Company ship, commission a regiment, or Tax. Building takes two successful checks: first place a partially built ship in the Governor’s region (if none is already there); a later success completes it into the associated President’s sea zone. Commission adds a regiment to that President’s Army. Tax adds £2, unsplit, to Balance or the President’s treasury; each Tax after the first that turn adds regional unrest. Every unsuccessful check adds unrest. The Governor may continue until choosing to stop, exhausting dice, or catastrophically failing (normal office removal applies).
answers.evidence: Governors: Administer: ‘reduce pool one after every result’; success benefits and ‘Every unsuccessful check adds unrest.’

answers.answer: Company expenses are £1 per Debt, each officer/regiment in an Army, and each ship in sea zones (including China); Commanders are excluded. If Balance is insufficient, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt one each until its track end, and continue receiving emergency loans even at maximum Debt. Newly added emergency Debt has no extra expense this turn. After emergency loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance with expectations under current Standing; if below, lower Standing one. After that the Chairman may pay any affordable number of dividends, costing £1 per Company share and paying each owner £1 per share, including the Chairman. If total dividend cash is strictly greater than expectations, raise Standing one. Standing at the leftmost space causes Company failure.
answers.evidence: Revenue: emergency loans ‘even at maximum Debt’; Standing losses for one/two or three-plus loans; then expectations and dividends.

answers.answer: An Invasion or Rebellion against a Company region triggers secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest. Resolve the primary attack first, then secondary attacks in Bombay, Madras and Bengal order; each Commander orders attacks within their Presidency. A normal primary Crisis attack strength is the usual Invasion/Rebellion strength plus unrest in its target. A primary Foreign Invasion instead uses only its ordinary attack die. Each secondary Rebellion’s strength is only the number of unrest cubes in that region, with no event modifier or empire strength. The associated Commander must exhaust active Army pieces totaling that strength, or as much as possible; alliances contribute printed strength and cannot be split. If defense strength is insufficient, Region Loss occurs: Commander returns half their family’s trophies rounded up, Commander returns to supply, officer losses are rolled, Governor and regional items are removed, dome/tower and flag are restored, control token returns loot-side down, and Standing falls by the number of regions lost so far this turn (first −1, second an additional −2, etc.). If defense is sufficient, clear all unrest in the attacked region and award the Commander one trophy; if it was a successful defense against a normal primary Invasion, also remove one tower from the attacker if possible. If Commander is vacant, Military Affairs acts in their stead, or Chairman if Military Affairs is vacant; that acting player chooses defense but gains/loses no trophies. A successful primary Invasion against the Company also applies empire growth.
answers.evidence: Attacks on Company: primary resolved first, then Bombay/Madras/Bengal; primary and secondary strengths; sufficient defense clears unrest and gives a trophy.

answers.answer: The PM reveals up to three laws one at a time, chooses one and discards the others; drawing a dilemma forces a selection and ends drawing. The PM chooses dial direction and stops at the first policy matching the law’s bottom icon, then sets the Vote marker to printed starting support. Starting with the PM and going clockwise, players vote using £1 family cash per vote plus printed card votes; support tracks are unlimited. The PM may call another full round or stop after a round, but a round with no votes ends voting. Players may change from supporting to opposing but cannot support after opposing; opposition totals identify the Opposition Leader, with a tied current holder retaining the title. At −1 or less the law fails and is discarded; any dilemma failure text resolves, the Opposition Leader returns the token and takes the PM dial, and the new PM moves the proposed policy one space either direction and resolves that adjacent policy. At zero or more the law passes, is placed with passed laws, the PM takes a passed-law token, and the selected policy resolves before immediate law effects. Used voting cards return to regular orientation after either result. If a law causes Company failure, finish the vote before scoring.
answers.evidence: Parliament Resolution: ‘−1 or less fails’; ‘Zero or higher passes’; passing resolves selected policy then immediate law effects.

answers.answer: In 1758 and Long 1710, at the start of a turn before London Season, the PM may call a special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. If it passes, reduce Debt by one per two current Debt, set Standing to S, give the PM a passed-law token, and activate firms. If it fails, increase Company-share scoring value by flipping/placing the Court VP token, up to ±3. This vote has no policy, does not remove the PM on failure, does not discard the Deregulation law, and the PM may vote against. The summary says 1813 starts deregulated; it does not describe a special vote there.
answers.evidence: Deregulation: PM ‘may call’ on lined and ‘must’ on starred conditions; pass/fail effects and exceptions stated.

answers.answer: In the Firms phase after Family share creation and before Hiring, a player may form a firm only if they currently manage none. They contribute one eligible Company share (returned to supply) or flip a workshop to its invested side, flip their family board, place a family member as the first firm share, set the value cube to the leftmost space, and take £5 from the bank into the London treasury. With a manager’s consent, an investor can make the same contribution to create a firm share and put £5 from the bank into London. A firm may have at most ten shares; further investments still add £5 but make no share. The Chairman’s share cannot be contributed. No Company shares may be invested if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and a share created this turn cannot be invested even if traded away. Invested workshops never revert to uninvested, and provide neither a bonus nor Company-failure VP, even if the firm fails. Family cash cannot be moved into or out of firm treasuries except through specified procedures.
answers.evidence: Firms phase: investments: ‘Form a firm — only if you currently manage none’; £5 to London; ten-share cap and investment restrictions.

answers.answer: Each manager secretly chooses a sea zone/home port and a London-cash bid; at least one ship is needed, and the home port may be closed. Hobnob is an alternative with no bid or trade/dividends, but it still pays expenses and retains the previous dividend marker. Bids are revealed simultaneously while strategies stay facedown until the associated Presidency begins. At the start of that Presidency, before office actions, each matching firm rolls one die per £1 bid and pays the bid to the bank; at least one 1 or 2 enables trade. Firm initiative equals ship count minus successful dice (1s/2s), and a President’s successful Trade uses the analogous Presidency ship count. After President succeeds, fill orders from lowest initiative up; the President picks ties. If the President is vacant or never trades successfully, firms fill after Commander/Governor actions and the Chairman breaks ties. A firm fills open orders up to ships + 1, starting at home port and tracing its own filled route; each order only once per firm. Orders can be refilled even if another firm or Company filled them, at half listed revenue rounded down. Firm India treasury receives revenue; the Value track advances one space per full £6 added to India treasury that turn.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies and competing trade: simultaneous bids, checks at Presidency start, initiative, order capacity and half revenue; Value advances per full £6.

answers.answer: At the start of Revenue, firms pay £1 per charter ship plus the higher of share count or firm Value, using either or both firm treasuries. If unable to pay, dissolve unless rescued. A dissolving firm’s shares go to Debtor’s Prison (each costs −1 VP), ships return to shipyards, and its charter returns to the family side; invested workshops remain invested. Rescue may use emergency investments under normal share/workshop rules (including the ten-share cap): pay expenses, lose remaining cash, and lower Value one space per emergency investment; alternatively merge with one other firm, which must pay its own expenses first if not yet paid and cover the failing firm’s unpaid expenses. After expenses, the manager may pay dividends only from India treasury. Each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to the manager; with manager consent, shareholders can forgo payment for any number of shares. Record total actual cash paid out on the Company Balance track. An active non-Hobnob firm that pays none records zero, while Hobnob retains its previous marker. Sweep remaining India money into London.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses, rescue and dividends: expense formula; dissolution destinations; India-only dividends and recorded total actual payout.
